subcategory_text: Supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management programs, and their performance is monitored throughout the technology product and service life cycle
informative_references: ISO/IEC 27001:2022: Clause 6.1.1, Clause 6.1.2, Annex A.5.19, Annex A.5.20, Annex A.5.21, Annex A.5.22
implementation_examples: Policies and procedures require provenance records for all acquired technology products and services
Periodically provide risk reporting to leaders about how acquired components are proven to be untampered and authentic

Communicate regularly among cybersecurity risk managers and operations personnel about the need to acquire software patches, updates, and upgrades only from authenticated and trustworthy software providers
Review policies to ensure that they require approved supplier personnel to perform maintenance on supplier products
Policies and procedure require checking upgrades to critical hardware for unauthorized changes
assessment_objectives: Determine whether supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management programs, and their performance is monitored throughout the technology product and service life cycle.
Determine whether mechanisms ensure that policies and procedures require provenance records for all acquired technology products and services.
Determine whether mechanisms ensure that periodically provide risk reporting to leaders about how acquired components are proven to be untampered and authentic.
Determine whether implementation outcomes are monitored, evaluated, and documented.
